steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
The requested language has no template that realizes Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples for this design; the R template is named
The interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error at 4 replicates per cell: power is low; state the power limitation beside the interaction results
Do not scale or transform the counts before the model — the size factor is applied as an offset inside the negative binomial model
FDR control holds within each contrast, not across the set of contrasts; the contrast name must accompany every adjusted p-value and gene list
steps.context: Inputs: T1S1 QC summary plus counts.csv and metadata.csv. User constraint: Python only — pydeseq2 0.5.4 is the pure-Python realization of the DESeq2 method of record (substitution); the R packages DESeq2 and ashr are NOT run. Execute tpl-pydeseq2-interaction@1.0.0 with these specifics: (1) Pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (smallest group size = 4); this sub-step has no Python template (the named template is R), so implement it directly in Python per those settings — minimal pre-filter only, independent filtering does the rest. (2) Model: pydeseq2 DESeqDataSet with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment; set reference levels EXPLICITLY: genotype = WT, treatment = vehicle (do not rely on alphabetical order). Fit the counts as delivered with NO length offset — the Salmon gene table has no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, so the import state is not established; do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input. No pre-normalization: median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model. (3) Test: Wald test of the interaction coefficient (genotype:treatment, the difference of drug effects KO minus WT — the research question) first; then the main-effect coefficients (treatment_drug_vs_vehicle = drug effect in WT; genotype_KO_vs_WT = genotype effect at vehicle). Compute the composite contrast drug effect in KO = treatment + interaction as an unshrunken linear combination with SE from the coefficient covariance matrix. (4) Shrinkage: inspect the installed pydeseq2 API first (its lfcShrink may or may not exist in 0.5.4). Shrink the single-coefficient estimates (interaction, treatment, genotype) with the available pure-Python shrinker (the procedure names ashr for the composite contrast; ashr is R-only and cannot be run under the Python-only constraint, so drug@KO is reported unshrunken with its SE). If no shrinker is available at all, report unshrunken log2FoldChange with lfcSE for every contrast and state in the output that shrinkage was unavailable in pure Python. (5) Multiple testing: Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast (FDR holds per contrast, not across contrasts), alpha = 0.05, independent filtering on with the same alpha; plot and inspect the p-value histogram before adjustment. (6) Outliers: keep the count-outlier behavior (cells with <7 replicates: Cook's-distance flag, p-values set to NA); report the number of flagged genes separately from independent-filter NAs. Save for the report step: one per-contrast results table (all genes: log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange where computed, pvalue, padj, contrast name), the drug@KO composite-contrast table, the p-value histogram, and a per-gene summary (mean normalized count, dispersion, log2FC and lfcSE per contrast) so T1S3 does not need the fitted model object.

steps.name: Report
caveats: The interaction coefficient alone does not say whether the drug has an effect at either level, and a simple effect alone does not say whether the effect differs between levels — the report must present all three together
Do not rank or plot by the unshrunken fold change of low-count genes; the unshrunken estimate is large and noisy for them
steps.context: Inputs: T1S2 per-contrast results tables, the drug@KO composite-contrast table, the per-gene summary (mean normalized count, dispersion, log2FC, lfcSE per contrast), and the p-value histogram. Assemble the report in Python (pandas, matplotlib). Interaction report per the DESeq2 vignette: for each gene, side by side, the drug effect at the reference genotype (drug@WT), the drug effect at the other level (drug@KO), and the interaction contrast (the difference of the two); name the reference level of each factor beside the table, because the meaning of each coefficient depends on it. Effect columns: log2FoldChange (unshrunken, from the test), shrunken log2FoldChange (where the shrinker ran), lfcSE; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value where available — the drug@KO composite column is unshrunken (ashr is R-only, unavailable under the Python-only constraint), so rank it by the Wald statistic and flag it as unshrunken. Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit (shrinkage changes estimates, not the test) and name the shrinkage estimator in the table headers. Fit diagnostics BEFORE the gene tables: MA plot and dispersion plot for the primary (interaction) contrast, each with a statement of what it shows. Robustness: the procedure recommends the overlap of DESeq2 and edgeR QL as a two-method check — the edgeR-QL half cannot be run under the user's Python-only constraint; state this omission explicitly in the report rather than presenting a single method as doubly validated. Report fields before the gene tables: method (DESeq2 method of record, realized via pydeseq2 0.5.4), package versions, design formula, reference levels, every contrast, thresholds (padj < 0.05), n genes tested after filtering, n DE genes per contrast, session info (versions, random seed). State the three limitations explicitly: (a) the Salmon length offset is lost because no length input was provided — changes in isoform use can appear as DE; (b) the interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large SE at 4 replicates per cell, so a non-significant interaction is not proof of equal drug effects; (c) the edgeR-QL robustness overlap is omitted because R is excluded by the user constraint.

plan.title: Heart 2x2 genotype-by-drug interaction DE
plan.analytical_narrative: 16 human heart samples in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug, 4 replicates per cell), Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes) with length-correction state unknown. The research question is the genotype x treatment interaction: does the drug act differently in the KO than in the WT. Logical flow: (1) design-blind sample structure QC (vst, PCA on top 500 variable genes, distance heatmap) to confirm the 2x2 separation and flag any outlier or swapped sample before testing; (2) minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples), then the DESeq2 method realized in pure Python via pydeseq2 (user constraint: Python only, no R): negative binomial model with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle), counts fitted as delivered with no length offset (no per-sample quantification files or length table exist, so the length offset is lost and must be stated); Wald test of the interaction coefficient first — that IS the research question — then the simple effects (drug@WT from the main effect, drug@KO as the unshrunken composite contrast treatment + interaction, genotype@vehicle); LFC shrinkage for single-coefficient contrasts with whatever shrinker the installed pydeseq2 0.5.4 exposes (the procedure names ashr for the composite contrast, but ashr is R-only and cannot be run under the Python-only constraint, so the composite contrast is reported unshrunken with its SE); Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. (3) A report giving, per gene, the drug effect in WT, the drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast side by side with reference levels named, MA and dispersion diagnostics before the gene tables, and explicit statements of the three limitations: lost Salmon length offset (isoform switches can appear as DE), limited power of the interaction test at 4 replicates per cell, and the omitted edgeR-QL robustness overlap because R is excluded by the user constraint.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA on top 500 variable genes + sample distance heatmap
minimal pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size (4) of samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the negative binomial model, no pre-normalized counts
DESeq2 negative binomial GLM with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle), gene counts imported without length offset
DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
ashr log fold change shrinkage (per procedure); in the Python-only environment realized by the pydeseq2 shrinker for single-coefficient contrasts, composite drug@KO contrast reported unshrunken
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, independent filtering on, alpha passed to the test
